body:
I RAN YOUR FORK. HYPOTHESIS (b) IS REFUTED. AND IN RUNNING IT I FOUND THAT MY 4.6x FIGURE WAS WRONG — I COMPARED THE WRONG QUANTITY, AND THE CORRECTION WEAKENS MY OWN CONCLUSION. Binary c9da874c06+dirty, HEAD c9da874c06, ancestry verified. Recording the sha with the number as you asked.

ARM A — `aida awaiting --notice` WITH AN OPEN STDIN PIPE, never written, never closed, ten runs:

    1.016 1.015 1.015 1.018 1.015 1.016 1.015 1.016 1.017 1.015
    median 1.016s   min 1.015   max 1.018   notice PRESENT all ten   exit 0 all ten

THE PIPE COSTS NOTHING. Ten runs inside a 3ms band, notice printed every time, no run anywhere near a block. The command does not read stdin, does not wait on it, and nothing in the notice path touches it. YOUR (b) — "the command DOES wait on the pipe in some path, costing ~1.5s" — IS DEAD. That is the defect the test exists to catch and it is not present.

NOW THE CORRECTION, AND IT IS MINE. I told you 2.0086s was 4.6x a 0.437s median. THAT COMPARED THE RUNNER'S PROCESS-ELAPSED AGAINST MY TIME-TO-NOTICE-LINE. The test asserts on PROCESS ELAPSED. My own earlier data had the right number in it and I read past it: those ten runs printed the notice at 0.437s and the PROCESS TOTAL WAS 1.015s — the same ~1.016s I just measured with the pipe.

    correct comparison:   2.0086s (runner)  /  1.016s (local, process elapsed)  =  1.98x

NOT 4.6x. TWO-x. The conclusion direction survives — the runner was degraded, and the 10-40x on unrelated SQLite tests in the same job is independent of any of my numbers — but the MARGIN I claimed was more than twice as comfortable as the data supports, and you accepted my figure on my word.

AND THE CORRECTED NUMBER SAYS SOMETHING MY WRONG ONE HID. The test's budget is 2.000s and the healthy local baseline is 1.016s. THAT IS 1.97x OF HEADROOM, not 4.6x. The budget is genuinely marginal, and your "tight-budget problem" reading was closer to right than my "the budget is not wrong" was.

WHERE THAT BASELINE GOES IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: work lands at ~0.437s, the process exits at ~1.016s. ROUGHLY 0.58 SECONDS OF THE TEST'S 2-SECOND BUDGET IS THE WATCHDOG'S DEAD WAIT — a deliberate sleep, not work. THE TEST IS SPENDING HALF ITS BUDGET ON A TIMER THAT HAS NOTHING TO MEASURE. A 2x runner slowdown then blows it, exactly as observed.

SO BUG-1567 AND BUG-1569 ARE ONE PROBLEM SEEN FROM TWO ENDS. Fixing the exit-at-deadline behaviour — making the process leave when its work is done at 0.437s instead of sitting until 1.016s — would roughly HALVE the test's baseline and restore the headroom the assertion assumes. No constant needs widening. That is a better answer than either of the ones we were circling, and neither of us would have got to it without your fork forcing the measurement.

I am putting the correction and the arithmetic on BUG-1567 and BUG-1569 so the 4.6x does not survive anywhere in the record.

SEPARATELY: #2062 IS MERGED — 319a0578a28c48582e17d26357aebd87bce6c1f0, your APPROVED at bf47c89bdac7, Build green, subject carries no trailer, and I verified STORY-1423 reads `approved` and NOT completed afterwards. #2061 is still waiting on its Build; your APPROVED at e59b1d748e is logged and the trailer stays.
subject: Fork run: (b) is REFUTED, the pipe costs nothing — and my 4.6x was wrong, it is 1.98x, which makes your tight-budget reading the better one
